title: a settings file with visualizationSettings kills the V key and the right-mouse dialog
author: Claude-JG
description: Reported by the maintainer against 1.12.96: with a ~/.exudyn/config.json holding a visualizationSettings section, pressing V in the render window opens no dialog and the console says 'problems with the SystemContainer, probably not attached to the renderer yet'. Without the file everything works. Reproduced and measured: revision2026b step RG12.10 installs a Python SUBCLASS as exudyn.SystemContainer when that section exists, and GUI.GetRendererSystemContainer() does isinstance(guiSC, exudyn.SystemContainer) on what the C++ side stores - MainSystemContainer.cpp does exudynModule.attr('sys')['currentRendererSystemContainer'] = this, a POINTER, which pybind casts to an object of the COMPILED class. isinstance of that against the subclass is False, so the probe returns None and every dialog that needs the container does nothing. This is the THIRD thing the subclass broke in two days: DefaultSettingsDictionary constructed it and reported the overrides as the defaults (#2684), an isinstance of mine in the settings dialog stopped recognising SC.visualizationSettings (#2685), and now this. The mechanism has to stop changing what a class is: the constructor of the compiled class is wrapped IN PLACE instead (measured: pybind11 heap types allow it), and then no name and no isinstance moves. The defaults then cannot be constructed any more - every construction applies the overrides - so they are snapshotted at import before the wrapper is installed, which is what was decided for exudyn.config in #2685. Two more things came with it, both asked for by the maintainer: GetRendererSystemContainer() said NOTHING when it failed, which is why this took a reproduction rather than a message - it now says once per process what went wrong, while the normal 'no renderer' answer stays quiet; and ShowVisualizationSettingsDialog printed 'ERROR: ShowRightMouseSelectionDialog: ...', a copy-paste error that named the wrong function in the one message a user sees. revision2026b step RG12.17.
releaseNotes: A settings file holding visualizationSettings no longer kills the dialogs. The cause was the Python subclass that RG12.10 installed as exudyn.SystemContainer: GUI.GetRendererSystemContainer() does isinstance() against that name on the object the C++ side stores as a pointer, which is of the COMPILED class, so the probe found nothing and the V key and the right-mouse dialog did nothing. The constructor of the compiled class is now wrapped IN PLACE instead of subclassed, so no name and no isinstance moves - the third thing that subclass broke in two days, and fixing the callers one at a time cannot work because the set of places that ask what a class is includes every user script. The defaults, which can then no longer be constructed, are snapshotted at import before the wrapper, as the defaults of exudyn.config are. Two things the maintainer asked for came with it: GetRendererSystemContainer() says once per process what went wrong instead of returning None in silence (the normal 'no renderer' answer stays quiet), and ShowVisualizationSettingsDialog no longer prints 'ERROR: ShowRightMouseSelectionDialog', a copy-paste error that named the wrong function in the one message a user sees. The 'strange position coordinates' [-10, 0] are not a defect: Windows reports the invisible resize border, and the reachability rule already allows screenX-16 for exactly that.
